newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast parliament elects new speaker.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast parliament elects new speaker.

text.p: Ivory Coast's lawmakers on Monday elected former cabinet minister Emile Brou Amoakon Atta as the new parliamentary speaker, deputies said.
Atta, 61, is a member of President Henri Konan Bedie's ruling Democratic Party and succeeds former speaker Charles Bauza Donwahi, who died on August 2.
Lawmakers said heavyweight politicians expected to vie for the post did not contest following new government constitutional review proposals that will erode the status of the job.

The assembly speaker is the constitutional interim successor to the head of state in the event of death or incapacitation. The speaker of a proposed senate or upper house will be the constitutional successor under the plans unveiled last Friday.
Atta received 139 votes -- all from the ruling party, which holds 149 of the 175 assembly seats. Twenty-six votes went to two opposition candidates.
